# ShipQuick UI component library

> Library components for Android (Compose Material 3), iOS (SwiftUI) and web. Build every screen from these components only; read a component's doc before you use it. Search and get them through the MCP server `shipquick_ui_mcp` (`python3 scripts/ui_mcp.py`). Generated by `python3 scripts/ui_mcp.py llms`; do not edit.

## Action

- [app-intents-and-app-shortcuts](components/app-intents-and-app-shortcuts/app-intents-and-app-shortcuts.doc.mjs): App Intents let Siri, Spotlight, Shortcuts and widgets run an action of the app. (ios)
- [Button](components/Button/Button.doc.mjs): A button starts an action when the user presses it. Use it to save, send, confirm or start a task. (android, ios, web)
- [ControlGroup](components/ControlGroup/ControlGroup.doc.mjs): ControlGroup shows a few related controls together, like zoom in and zoom out. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [controls](components/controls/controls.doc.mjs): A control is a button or toggle of the app in Control Center, on the Lock Screen or on the Action button. (ios)
- [FloatingActionButton](components/FloatingActionButton/FloatingActionButton.doc.mjs): A floating action button (FAB) is a high-emphasis button for the one main action on a screen, like a new note. It sits at the bottom right. Small, large and extended (icon plus words) FABs exist too. (android)
- [IconButton](components/IconButton/IconButton.doc.mjs): An icon button is an action shown as one icon. Use it for common actions, like open a menu or search. A toggle icon button turns something on or off, like favorite. (android, web)
- [quick-actions](components/quick-actions/quick-actions.doc.mjs): Quick actions are the short menu people see when they press and hold the app icon. (ios)
- [ShareLink](components/ShareLink/ShareLink.doc.mjs): ShareLink is a share button. It opens the system share sheet. Apple: "A view that controls a sharing presentation." (ios)

## Container

- [Card](components/Card/Card.doc.mjs): A card holds one piece of content, like a product, a news story or a message. (android, ios, web)
- [DisclosureGroup](components/DisclosureGroup/DisclosureGroup.doc.mjs): DisclosureGroup shows or hides more content when people tap its title. Apple: "A view that shows or hides another content view, based on the state of a disclosure control." (ios)
- [Surface](components/Surface/Surface.doc.mjs): Surface is the base container under cards, sheets and bars: shape, colour, elevation and border. It also sets the content colour for what is inside. (android)

## Content

- [Carousel](components/Carousel/Carousel.doc.mjs): A carousel is a list of items the user scrolls sideways, sized to the window. It is for related visual content, like photos. (android, web)
- [Icon](components/Icon/Icon.doc.mjs): An icon is a small picture that stands for an action or a thing. Material 3 tints it with the content colour of what is behind it. (android)
- [Image](components/Image/Image.doc.mjs): Image shows one picture: an asset from the app, a photo, or an SF Symbol. Apple: "A view that displays an image." (ios)
- [Text](components/Text/Text.doc.mjs): Text shows read-only words, one line or many. (android, ios)
- [web-view](components/web-view/web-view.doc.mjs): A web view shows a web page inside the app. (ios)
- [widgets](components/widgets/widgets.doc.mjs): A widget shows a small, glanceable view of the app outside the app. (android, ios)

## Data Input

- [DatePicker](components/DatePicker/DatePicker.doc.mjs): A date picker lets the user pick a date. (android, ios)
- [DateRangePicker](components/DateRangePicker/DateRangePicker.doc.mjs): DateRangePicker lets the user pick a start date and an end date, like the days of a trip. (android)
- [SearchBar](components/SearchBar/SearchBar.doc.mjs): A search field lets the user type words to find results in the app. (android, ios)
- [TextField](components/TextField/TextField.doc.mjs): A text field lets the user type and change text. (android, ios, web)
- [TimePicker](components/TimePicker/TimePicker.doc.mjs): A time picker lets the user pick a time. TimePicker is a dial. TimeInput uses the keyboard. Both take a TimePickerState, and both show in a dialog. (android)

## Data Visualization

- [activity-rings](components/activity-rings/activity-rings.doc.mjs): Activity rings show Move, Exercise and Stand progress. (ios)
- [swift-charts](components/swift-charts/swift-charts.doc.mjs): Charts show data as bars, lines, points or areas. (ios)

## Feedback & Status

- [Badge](components/Badge/Badge.doc.mjs): A badge is a small mark on another part that shows a status or a number, like unread messages or items in a cart. (android, ios, web)
- [ContentUnavailableView](components/ContentUnavailableView/ContentUnavailableView.doc.mjs): ContentUnavailableView tells people there is nothing to show yet, like no search results. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [Gauge](components/Gauge/Gauge.doc.mjs): Gauge shows one number inside a range, like a battery level. Apple: "A view that shows a value within a range." (ios)
- [live-activities](components/live-activities/live-activities.doc.mjs): A Live Activity shows the live state of a task, like a delivery, on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. (ios)
- [notifications](components/notifications/notifications.doc.mjs): A notification tells people about something new while the app is closed. (android, ios)
- [ProgressIndicator](components/ProgressIndicator/ProgressIndicator.doc.mjs): A progress indicator shows that work is going on, like loading data or an upload. Determinate shows how much is done. Indeterminate moves until the work ends. (android, ios, web)
- [Snackbar](components/Snackbar/Snackbar.doc.mjs): Snackbar is the message itself: a short line with an optional action and close button. SnackbarHost shows it for you. Call it directly only to change how the host draws each one. (android)
- [SnackbarHost](components/SnackbarHost/SnackbarHost.doc.mjs): A snackbar is a short message at the bottom of the screen, like "Message deleted" with Undo. It does not stop the user. (android, web)

## Form Controls

- [Checkbox](components/Checkbox/Checkbox.doc.mjs): A checkbox lets the user pick one or more items from a list, turn an item on or off, or agree to terms. (android, web)
- [Chip](components/Chip/Chip.doc.mjs): A chip is a small part with a label and often an icon. Assist chips guide a task. Filter chips narrow content and can be selected. Input chips show what the user entered and can be removed. Suggestion chips offer next steps. (android)
- [ColorPicker](components/ColorPicker/ColorPicker.doc.mjs): ColorPicker opens the system colour picker and shows the chosen colour. Apple: "A control used to select a color from the system color picker UI." (ios)
- [Form](components/Form/Form.doc.mjs): Form groups controls for data entry, like a settings screen. LabeledContent shows a label next to a value. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [OutlinedTextField](components/OutlinedTextField/OutlinedTextField.doc.mjs): OutlinedTextField is a text field with a border and no fill. Use it when filled fields look too heavy, for example in a long form. (android)
- [Picker](components/Picker/Picker.doc.mjs): Picker lets people choose one value from a set. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [RadioButton](components/RadioButton/RadioButton.doc.mjs): A radio button lets the user pick one option from a set. Put each RadioButton and its label in a Row. (android)
- [SecureTextField](components/SecureTextField/SecureTextField.doc.mjs): SecureTextField is a filled text field for a password. It hides what the user types. (android)
- [SegmentedButton](components/SegmentedButton/SegmentedButton.doc.mjs): A segmented button lets the user pick from a few options set side by side. (android, ios, web)
- [Slider](components/Slider/Slider.doc.mjs): A slider lets the user pick a value from a range, like volume, a price range or a rating. It has a track, a thumb and optional tick marks. (android, ios, web)
- [Stepper](components/Stepper/Stepper.doc.mjs): Stepper has a minus and a plus segment that change a number by a step. Apple: "A control that performs increment and decrement actions." (ios)
- [Switch](components/Switch/Switch.doc.mjs): A switch turns one thing on or off, like a setting or a feature. The user drags the thumb or taps the switch. (android, ios, web)

## Layout

- [BottomSheetScaffold](components/BottomSheetScaffold/BottomSheetScaffold.doc.mjs): BottomSheetScaffold is a screen layout with a standard bottom sheet. The sheet stays on screen beside the content, partly or fully open, like a map with a list. (android)
- [Divider](components/Divider/Divider.doc.mjs): A divider is a thin line between items in a list or other container. (android, ios, web)
- [Grid](components/Grid/Grid.doc.mjs): Grid places views in rows and columns. Lazy grids make only the cells on screen. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [LayoutModifiers](components/LayoutModifiers/LayoutModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers that set a view's size and place. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Scaffold](components/Scaffold/Scaffold.doc.mjs): Scaffold is the frame of a screen. It holds the top app bar, the bottom bar, the floating action button and the snackbar host in their right places. (android)
- [ScrollView](components/ScrollView/ScrollView.doc.mjs): ScrollView lets people move content that is bigger than the screen. Apple: "A scrollable view." (ios)
- [Stacks](components/Stacks/Stacks.doc.mjs): Stacks place views in a row, a column, or on top of each other. Spacer pushes views apart. These are layout containers. Rule 38 allows them. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)

## Navigation

- [AppBar](components/AppBar/AppBar.doc.mjs): An app bar gives access to key tasks and navigation. A top app bar has the title, main actions and navigation. A bottom app bar has core navigation or actions. (android, ios)
- [AppBarColumn](components/AppBarColumn/AppBarColumn.doc.mjs): AppBarColumn lays out app bar actions in a column, for example in a vertical toolbar. Items that do not fit move into an overflow menu. (android)
- [AppBarRow](components/AppBarRow/AppBarRow.doc.mjs): AppBarRow lays out the actions of an app bar in a row. Items that do not fit move into an overflow menu. (android)
- [Link](components/Link/Link.doc.mjs): Link opens a web address or an app link. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [NavigationBar](components/NavigationBar/NavigationBar.doc.mjs): A navigation bar at the bottom lets the user switch between the app's main places. (android, ios)
- [NavigationDrawer](components/NavigationDrawer/NavigationDrawer.doc.mjs): A navigation drawer lists many sections, account links, or features in a complex app. (android, ios)
- [NavigationRail](components/NavigationRail/NavigationRail.doc.mjs): A navigation rail sits on the side of a large screen and gives access to the main places. Each NavigationRailItem is one place. (android)
- [NavigationSplitView](components/NavigationSplitView/NavigationSplitView.doc.mjs): NavigationSplitView shows two or three columns. A choice in one column shows its content in the next. Apple: "A view that presents views in two or three columns, where selections in leading columns control presentations in subsequent columns." (ios)
- [NavigationStack](components/NavigationStack/NavigationStack.doc.mjs): NavigationStack shows one screen at a time. A NavigationLink pushes the next screen. The back button goes back. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [PageControl](components/PageControl/PageControl.doc.mjs): A page control is the row of dots under swipeable pages. In SwiftUI it is a TabView with the page style. Apple: "A TabViewStyle that displays a paged scrolling TabView." (ios)
- [ShortNavigationBar](components/ShortNavigationBar/ShortNavigationBar.doc.mjs): ShortNavigationBar is the newer, shorter bottom bar for three to five top destinations of an app. (android)
- [Tab](components/Tab/Tab.doc.mjs): A Tab is one tab in a tab row. It shows text, an icon or both, and it is selected or not. (android)
- [Tabs](components/Tabs/Tabs.doc.mjs): Tabs group related content. Primary tabs sit under the top app bar and show the main content. Secondary tabs split content further inside an area. (android, web)
- [WideNavigationRail](components/WideNavigationRail/WideNavigationRail.doc.mjs): WideNavigationRail is the newer rail for medium and large screens. It is collapsed (icons only) or expanded (icons with labels, like a drawer). (android)

## Overlay

- [BottomSheet](components/BottomSheet/BottomSheet.doc.mjs): A modal bottom sheet slides up from the bottom over the screen, with more content or actions. (android, ios, web)
- [ContactAccess](components/ContactAccess/ContactAccess.doc.mjs): Modifiers for limited contact access: the picker where people choose which contacts the app may see, and the look of the contact access button. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier from ContactsUI. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [DatePickerDialog](components/DatePickerDialog/DatePickerDialog.doc.mjs): DatePickerDialog holds a DatePicker in a dialog, with confirm and dismiss buttons. Use it when the user picks a date from a form. (android)
- [Dialog](components/Dialog/Dialog.doc.mjs): A dialog shows a message or asks for input on a layer above the app. It stops the user on purpose. Use it to confirm an action, like deleting a file, or to ask a short question. (android, ios, web)
- [edit-menus](components/edit-menus/edit-menus.doc.mjs): An edit menu shows Copy, Paste and other edit actions. (ios)
- [FileDialogs](components/FileDialogs/FileDialogs.doc.mjs): Modifiers that present the system file dialogs: import, export and move a file, plus the options of those dialogs. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Label](components/TooltipLabel/TooltipLabel.doc.mjs): Label adds a small label tooltip to its content. It shows when the user hovers, focuses or long-presses the content. (android)
- [Menu](components/Menu/Menu.doc.mjs): A drop-down menu opens from an icon, a text field or another part and shows a list of options on a short-lived surface. It can have dividers and icons. (android, ios, web)
- [PhotosPicker](components/PhotosPicker/PhotosPicker.doc.mjs): Modifiers that present the system Photos picker and the shared album sheets from PhotosUI, and set the picker's look. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Popover](components/Popover/Popover.doc.mjs): A popover is a short-lived view over the screen, pointing at the control that opened it. On iPhone it shows as a sheet. Apple: "Presents a popover when a given condition is true." (ios)
- [PresentationModifiers](components/PresentationModifiers/PresentationModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers that present system screens no other doc covers, like a Quick Look preview or a translation popover. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [TimePickerDialog](components/TimePickerDialog/TimePickerDialog.doc.mjs): TimePickerDialog holds a TimePicker or TimeInput in a dialog, with a title, confirm and dismiss buttons and an optional mode toggle. (android)
- [Tooltip](components/Tooltip/Tooltip.doc.mjs): A tooltip adds a short note to a button or other part. A plain tooltip says what an icon button does. A rich tooltip says more and can have a title, a link and buttons. (android, ios, web)

## Table & List

- [collection-view](components/collection-view/collection-view.doc.mjs): A collection view shows many items in a custom layout. (ios)
- [List](components/List/List.doc.mjs): A list shows a set of items. (android, ios, web)
- [pull-to-refresh](components/pull-to-refresh/pull-to-refresh.doc.mjs): Pull to refresh lets people reload a scrolling list by pulling it down. (android)
- [SwipeToDismissBox](components/SwipeToDismissBox/SwipeToDismissBox.doc.mjs): SwipeToDismissBox lets the user swipe an item to the side to act on it, like delete. The background content shows behind the item while it moves. (android)
- [Table](components/Table/Table.doc.mjs): Table shows rows of data in columns. On iPhone it shows only the first column. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)

## Utility

- [AccessibilityActions](components/AccessibilityActions/AccessibilityActions.doc.mjs): Modifiers that give VoiceOver and other assistive tools custom actions on a view: named actions, adjust, scroll, zoom and quick actions. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [AccessibilityModifiers](components/AccessibilityModifiers/AccessibilityModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers that tell VoiceOver and other assistive tools what a view is and does. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [AccessibilityRotors](components/AccessibilityRotors/AccessibilityRotors.doc.mjs): Modifiers that add a custom VoiceOver rotor and its entries, so a user can jump between related items. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Animators](components/Animators/Animators.doc.mjs): These types and modifiers animate views or redraw them on a schedule. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [AppearanceModifiers](components/AppearanceModifiers/AppearanceModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers that change how a view looks: its colors, its background, or if it shows. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Canvas](components/Canvas/Canvas.doc.mjs): Canvas draws shapes, text and images by code, one frame at a time. App screens are built from library components, so app code does not draw its own UI. Canvas is for a chart or a game surface that no library component covers. (ios)
- [ColorAdjustments](components/ColorAdjustments/ColorAdjustments.doc.mjs): Modifiers that adjust the colors a view draws: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, invert, grayscale and multiply. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [DocumentLaunchView](components/DocumentLaunchView/DocumentLaunchView.doc.mjs): DocumentLaunchView is the first screen of an app that opens documents, with a button to make a new one or open one. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [DragAndDrop](components/DragAndDrop/DragAndDrop.doc.mjs): Modifiers that start a drag, take a drop, or reorder items. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Focus](components/Focus/Focus.doc.mjs): Modifiers that move, read or share focus: which view takes keyboard and hardware input next. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Gestures](components/Gestures/Gestures.doc.mjs): Modifiers that make a view answer touches: taps, long presses, custom gestures, hit testing and Apple Pencil input. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Glass](components/Glass/Glass.doc.mjs): Liquid Glass is the system glass material. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [Gradient](components/Gradient/Gradient.doc.mjs): Color and the gradient types are views and fills. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [GraphicsModifiers](components/GraphicsModifiers/GraphicsModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers that change how a view is drawn: clip, blur, shadow, turn or scale. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Hover](components/Hover/Hover.doc.mjs): Modifiers for a pointer over a view: hover effects and hover actions on iPad with a trackpad or mouse. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [ImagePlayground](components/ImagePlayground/ImagePlayground.doc.mjs): Modifiers for the Image Playground sheet: present it, and pick its styles and options. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [InAppPurchase](components/InAppPurchase/InAppPurchase.doc.mjs): Modifiers for StoreKit's store, product and subscription views: offers, tasks that load products and entitlements, and the look of the subscription store. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier from StoreKit. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [InputModifiers](components/InputModifiers/InputModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers for view events and other input that no control doc owns: appear and disappear, value changes, open URLs, user activity, game controllers, cameras and visionOS or watchOS input. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. Gestures, Focus, Keyboard, DragAndDrop and Hover have their own docs. (ios)
- [Keyboard](components/Keyboard/Keyboard.doc.mjs): Modifiers that answer a hardware keyboard: key presses, shortcuts and system commands. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. The on-screen keyboard belongs to TextField. (ios)
- [Map](components/Map/Map.doc.mjs): Modifiers for MapKit's Map view: style, controls, camera, feature selection, map item details and Look Around. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier from MapKit. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [MaterialTheme](components/MaterialTheme/MaterialTheme.doc.mjs): MaterialTheme gives every Material 3 part below it the same colours, type and shapes. Wrap the whole app in it once. Build its colour scheme, type scale and shapes from the tokens in design/tokens.json. (android)
- [Redaction](components/Redaction/Redaction.doc.mjs): Modifiers that hide content as a placeholder, mark it private, or block screen capture of it. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [ShaderEffects](components/ShaderEffects/ShaderEffects.doc.mjs): Modifiers that run a Metal shader on a view or read its geometry to change how it draws. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Shape](components/Shape/Shape.doc.mjs): Shapes fill or stroke a simple form, like a circle behind an icon. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [ShapePlumbing](components/ShapePlumbing/ShapePlumbing.doc.mjs): These types wrap a shape after you fill, stroke, move, turn or scale it. SwiftUI makes them for you. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [Spatial](components/Spatial/Spatial.doc.mjs): Modifiers for visionOS: spatial overlays, the surroundings effect, hand visibility and the volume baseplate. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Speech](components/Speech/Speech.doc.mjs): Modifiers that shape how VoiceOver and other speech output read a view aloud: pitch, punctuation, spelling and announcement queueing. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [StateModifiers](components/StateModifiers/StateModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers that pass data down or up the view tree. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [TechnologyModifiers](components/TechnologyModifiers/TechnologyModifiers.doc.mjs): Modifiers from other Apple frameworks that have no doc of their own: HealthKit, WorkoutKit, MusicKit, RealityKit, Core Motion, Core Location, Nearby Interaction, device management, Sign in with Apple and the music, journaling and transaction pickers. StoreKit, MapKit, TipKit, PassKit and Image Playground rows live in their own docs. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Tips](components/Tips/Tips.doc.mjs): Modifiers for TipKit tips: a popover tip on a view and the look of a TipView. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier from TipKit. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [Transforms3D](components/Transforms3D/Transforms3D.doc.mjs): Modifiers that rotate, project, scale and lay out a view in three dimensions. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [ViewPlumbing](components/ViewPlumbing/ViewPlumbing.doc.mjs): These types hold views together. They draw nothing of their own. SwiftUI makes most of them for you. Use the SwiftUI type as Apple ships it. Do not redraw it. (ios)
- [Wallet](components/Wallet/Wallet.doc.mjs): Modifiers for PassKit's Apple Pay and Wallet buttons: payment sheet callbacks, pay later views, add-to-Wallet and verify-identity buttons. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier from PassKit. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)
- [WindowBehavior](components/WindowBehavior/WindowBehavior.doc.mjs): Modifiers that set how a window resizes, minimizes, goes full screen and dismisses, plus its clipping margins. Each entry is a SwiftUI view modifier. Add it to a view as Apple ships it. (ios)

## Custom components

- None yet.
